title: Accessibility audit
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for auditing a web page or app against WCAG 2.2 level AA: keyboard paths, focus order and visibility, contrast, text alternatives, captions and transcripts, reflow at 320 CSS pixels, target size, reduced motion, language and landmarks, with every finding citing its success criterion, and tested code for contrast ratios and landmark and heading order.
boundaries: Every finding cites one WCAG 2.2 success criterion and says failure or advisory; AAA criteria are advisory in an AA audit.
Captures and keyboard walks are read-only: no form is submitted, nothing is typed into fields and no account is created.
A report never claims conformance; it states what was checked and what was not.
A person's assistive-technology session is a person's verb; the audit review is by a different worker.
The pack's code reads files it is given and prints results; it opens no network connection and calls no model.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing, enqueues nothing and installs no code.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for auditing a page or app against WCAG 2.2 level AA

value.lets_workers: Plan an audit across pages, states, widths, themes and input modes; capture each state read-only; check contrast, structure, keyboard paths, reflow, target size, media, motion and text alternatives; have a person try the key tasks with assistive technology; and write a report whose every finding cites its WCAG success criterion, says failure or advisory and states what was not checked.

flow.when: Once per plan; deterministic and read-only.
On the captures, in every theme; deterministic.
On the rendered DOM snapshots; deterministic.
On the live pages, keyboard only.
At 320 CSS pixels and with wider text spacing; deterministic.
For every video and audio element.
With and without reduced motion; deterministic.
For images, icons, controls and fields.
A person tries the key tasks with a screen reader; a person's verb.
A different worker or a person rechecks a sample.

guardrails: Every finding cites one success criterion by number, name and level, and says whether it is a failure or advisory.
AAA criteria and best practices are advisory in an AA audit; they never make a page fail.
Automated checks find only part of the problems. A report never claims the site is compliant or fully accessible; it says what was checked and what was not.
Captures and walks are read-only: no form is submitted, nothing is typed into fields and no account is created.
A person's assistive-technology session is its own verb; an agent never reports one it did not have.
complements: The public-good kits pack's check-accessibility covers kit documents; this pack covers web pages and apps.
The visual and 3D rendering pack's contrast example covers rendered graphics; this pack ships the tested contrast tool.
Every failure goes to the findings to fixes pack for its fix, verification and guard.

nouns.title: How an accessibility audit is planned, checked, reported and reviewed
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: plan-audit names the pages, states, widths, themes, input modes and the criteria in scope.
capture-states saves a screenshot and a rendered DOM snapshot of every planned cell, by digest.
Each check verb covers its own area and cites a criterion for every result.
check-with-assistive-tech: a person tries the key tasks with a screen reader.
write-audit-report turns failures and advisories into findings and states what was not checked.
review-audit: a different worker or a person reproduces a sample before anyone relies on the report.
rules: Every finding cites one success criterion: number, name and level, with failure or advisory.
In an AA audit, AAA criteria and best practices are advisory.
Evidence names the address, the state, the width and the theme, and stores screenshots by SHA-256 with the region that shows the problem.
cannot_tell is an honest result; a check never guesses pass.

The report's statement follows from its parts: failures_found when any failure exists; no_failures_found_in_what_was_checked only when nothing in scope went unchecked and a person's assistive-technology session ran; otherwise not_claimed.
Never write that a site is compliant, certified or fully accessible.

severity.P1: A failure that stops some people from finishing a key task, such as a keyboard trap or a video with no captions.
severity.P2: A failure that makes a task hard or slow, such as low contrast on secondary text or a small target with a workaround.
severity.P3: An advisory, or a failure on a minor part with an easy workaround.
severity.P0: Not an accessibility level: route exposed personal data or credentials to the security review pack.

sources: W3C Website Accessibility Conformance Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM) 1.0, a W3C Working Group Note: scope, explore, sample, audit, report. The steps here are written for this pack.

nouns.title: WCAG 2.2, the W3C Recommendation this audit cites
nouns.category_reason: A public standard, cited by number and linked, never copied.

value.name: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
value.publication_status: W3C Recommendation, first published 5 October 2023. Read the dated version at the address before relying on it.
notes: WCAG 2.2 added nine success criteria, including 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum), 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), 3.2.6 Consistent Help, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry and 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum).
4.1.1 Parsing is obsolete in WCAG 2.2 and is not audited here.
The criteria's wording belongs to the W3C under its document license; this pack paraphrases and links instead of copying.

nouns.title: WCAG 2.2 A and AA criteria this audit checks, by area
nouns.category_reason: A fixed checklist every audited page is checked against.

criteria.name: Keyboard
criteria.asks: Every action works from a keyboard alone, with no timing needed.

criteria.name: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.asks: Focus can always leave a part with the keyboard, or the page says how.

criteria.name: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.asks: A single-key shortcut can be turned off or remapped, or works only while its part has focus.

criteria.name: Bypass Blocks
criteria.asks: A skip link, landmarks or headings let people jump past repeated blocks.

criteria.name: Focus Order
criteria.asks: Focus moves in an order that keeps meaning and operation.

criteria.name: Focus Visible
criteria.asks: The keyboard focus indicator is visible at every stop.

criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.asks: A focused part is never entirely hidden by sticky headers, banners or other author content.

criteria.name: On Focus
criteria.asks: Focus alone never changes the context, such as opening a new page.

criteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.asks: Text has 4.5:1 against its background, or 3:1 when large, in every theme.

criteria.name: Non-text Contrast
criteria.asks: Control boundaries, focus indicators and meaningful graphics have 3:1 against what is next to them.

criteria.name: Use of Color
criteria.asks: Color is never the only way information or an action is shown.

criteria.name: Non-text Content
criteria.asks: Images, icons and controls have text alternatives that serve the same purpose; decoration is hidden.

criteria.name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.asks: Audio-only has a transcript; video-only has a transcript or an audio track.

criteria.name: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.asks: Prerecorded video with sound has synchronized captions.

criteria.name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.asks: Prerecorded video has audio description or a full text alternative.

criteria.name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.asks: Prerecorded video has audio description, unless the main audio already conveys every important visual.

criteria.name: Audio Control
criteria.asks: Sound that plays on its own for more than three seconds can be paused or turned down.

criteria.name: Reflow
criteria.asks: At 320 CSS pixels wide, content reads without horizontal scrolling, except content that needs two dimensions.

criteria.name: Resize Text
criteria.asks: Text can grow to 200 percent without losing content or function.

criteria.name: Text Spacing
criteria.asks: Wider line, paragraph, letter and word spacing loses no content.

criteria.name: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.asks: Content shown on hover or focus can be dismissed, hovered and stays until dismissed.

criteria.name: Orientation
criteria.asks: Content works in portrait and landscape unless one is essential.

criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.asks: Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or meet one of the exceptions.

criteria.name: Dragging Movements
criteria.asks: Anything done by dragging can also be done with single pointer actions.

criteria.name: Label in Name
criteria.asks: A control's accessible name contains its visible label text.

criteria.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.asks: Motion that starts on its own and lasts more than five seconds can be paused, stopped or hidden.

criteria.name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.asks: Nothing flashes more than three times in any second, unless below the flash thresholds.

criteria.name: Language of Page
criteria.asks: The page states its main language.

criteria.name: Language of Parts
criteria.asks: Passages in another language are marked with their language.

criteria.name: Info and Relationships
criteria.asks: Headings, lists, landmarks, tables and labels are in the markup, not only in the look.

criteria.name: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.asks: The reading order in the markup keeps the meaning.

criteria.name: Page Titled
criteria.asks: Each page has a title that says what it is.

criteria.name: Headings and Labels
criteria.asks: Headings and labels describe their topic or purpose.

criteria.name: Name, Role, Value
criteria.asks: Every control exposes its name, role and state.

criteria.name: Labels or Instructions
criteria.asks: Fields that need input have labels or instructions.

criteria.name: Error Identification
criteria.asks: An input error is identified and described in text.

criteria.name: Status Messages
criteria.asks: Status messages are announced without moving focus.

criteria.name: Redundant Entry
criteria.asks: Information already entered in a process is filled in or selectable, not asked again.

criteria.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.asks: Signing in needs no memory or puzzle test unless an alternative or help is given.

criteria.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.asks: Each link's purpose is clear from its text or its context.

criteria.name: Multiple Ways
criteria.asks: A page can be found in more than one way, such as navigation and a site map.

criteria.name: Consistent Navigation
criteria.asks: Repeated navigation appears in the same order on every page.

criteria.name: Consistent Help
criteria.asks: Help or contact options appear in the same place on every page.

method_meaning.manual: A person or a careful agent judges it.
method_meaning.both: A tool finds candidates and a person or agent confirms them.

value.not_listed: Other A and AA criteria still apply; a plan that leaves one out lists it under not_in_scope with the reason.

nouns.title: Which states, widths, themes and settings to capture
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call rule for which cells to capture and check.

cells.themes: Every theme the surface offers, such as light and dark

checks_per_cell.structure: Once per page and state, on the rendered DOM
checks_per_cell.reflow: 320, light theme, plus wider text spacing

states: Menus, dialogs and disclosures opened by keyboard
Error and empty states reachable without submitting real data
value.screenshots: Full page and viewport, PNG, stored by SHA-256; a region is [x, y, width, height] in CSS pixels of the full-page image.
never: Submit a form, type into a field or create an account to reach a state.
Use real personal data in any state.

nouns.title: Walking a page with the keyboard alone
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call procedure: the same page and keys give the same walk.

per_stop: The focused element's name, role and box
Whether the focus indicator is visible: crops of the stop focused and unfocused differ
Whether it is obscured: the element at the center of its box is the focused one
Whether the order follows the reading order
page_checks: The first stop is a skip link that moves focus to the main content.
Escape closes menus and dialogs and returns focus to what opened them.
No trap: focus leaves every part within a few presses. Native media controls may hold several stops; count until focus leaves.
Single-character shortcuts (2.1.4) can be turned off or remapped, or act only while their part has focus.
Every action reachable by pointer is reachable by keyboard (2.1.1).
never: Press Enter on a submit button or type into a field during an audit walk.
Refocus an element in a way that resets its inner controls and then report a trap.
keys: Space on buttons that change display only

nouns.title: Measuring contrast from computed styles
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call measurement rule implemented by the pack's tested code.

value.pairs: Take each text element's computed color and the nearest opaque background behind it, compositing transparent layers over the page canvas.
value.large_text: At least 24 CSS pixels, or at least 18.67 CSS pixels (14 point) and bold (weight 700 or more). Unknown size is judged as normal text.
value.rounding: Pass and fail use the unrounded ratio. Reports show two decimals.
value.cannot_tell: Text over an image or gradient is cannot_tell unless measured at its lightest and darkest points.
exempt: Text that is not visible to anyone, such as an off-screen skip link until it is focused; check it focused

nouns.title: Reflow, text spacing and target size rules
nouns.category_reason: Zero-call geometric rules for three criteria.

reflow.pass: No horizontal scrolling of the page at 320 CSS pixels, and no content or function lost.
two_dimensional_exceptions: Code samples with long lines inside their own scroll box

text_spacing.pass: No text is clipped, overlapped or lost with all four applied. Visually hidden helper text with a 1-pixel box is not clipped content.

exceptions_in_order: Spacing: a 24-pixel circle centered on the target touches no other target or circle
Equivalent: another control on the page does the same and meets the size
Inline: the target sits in a sentence or block of text
User agent: the browser draws it unchanged
Essential: the size is required or legally fixed
target_size.measure: The bounding box of the clickable area; a label tied to a checkbox adds its area.

nouns.title: Checking video, audio and motion
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call checklist for media and motion criteria.

video: Captions (1.2.2): a captions track in the spoken language that loads, covers the whole running time and matches a sample of the narration.
Audio description (1.2.5): a described version or descriptions track, or a record that the narration already conveys every important visual; say which, and who judged it.
Media alternative (1.2.3): a full text alternative with the speech and the important visuals also satisfies level A; a transcript of speech alone does not.
Controls: play, pause, volume and captions work by keyboard and have names.
Sound that starts on its own for more than three seconds can be paused or muted (1.4.2).
motion: Motion that starts on its own and lasts more than five seconds has a pause, stop or hide control (2.2.2).
Flashing (2.3.1) is cannot_tell unless measured with a named flash analysis tool.
Honoring prefers-reduced-motion is advisory under 2.3.3 (AAA) in an AA audit.

nouns.title: The structure linter's rules and the criteria they relate to
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call rule list; the pack's code tests keep it equal to the linter's own rules.

limits: The linter reads markup, not style sheets: content hidden only by a style sheet still counts as visible.
Run it on a rendered DOM snapshot for pages built by scripts.
Language of parts (3.1.2) is not linted; it needs a reader.

nouns.title: Tool card: the accessibility checks
nouns.category_reason: Tested code a worker runs inside a claimed verb, pinned by path, file count and digest.

value.name: accessibility checks
value.runtime: Python 3.10 or later, standard library only; nothing to install.
commands: python -m a11y_checks contrast FOREGROUND BACKGROUND [--size-px N] [--weight W] [--non-text]
does: Contrast ratios for text (1.4.3, with 1.4.6 reported separately) and non-text parts (1.4.11), with alpha compositing and the large-text rule.
Landmark, heading-order, page-language and page-title lint, each result citing its criterion and marked failure or advisory.
does_not: Render pages, run page scripts or load style sheets.
Open a network connection, call a model or write any file.
Decide conformance; it reports measurements for a worker's check verb.
value.tests: The code's tests check published reference ratios and every lint rule, and recompute this pack's two worked examples from source.json, in the library's CI job for the pack.

nouns.title: SYNTHETIC worked example: theme colors in light and dark
nouns.category_reason: A golden fixture the validator and the pack's contrast tool both recompute.

value.purpose: Synthetic theme colors checked in both themes, recomputed by the library validator and again by this pack's contrast tool in its own CI job.
value.formula: Relative luminance L = 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B of linearized sRGB channels (c/12.92 at or below 0.04045, else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ^ 2.4); ratio = (L_lighter + 0.05) / (L_darker + 0.05).
reading: normal_text is the 1.4.3 threshold for text under 24 pixels, or under 18.67 pixels when bold; large_text is the 3:1 threshold for larger text.
The same 3:1 value is the 1.4.11 threshold for control boundaries and focus indicators, a different criterion.
A token that passes in one theme can fail in the other: check every theme a surface offers.

nouns.title: SYNTHETIC worked example: landmark, heading and language lint
nouns.category_reason: A golden fixture of pages and expected lint results.

value.purpose: Five small synthetic pages and the rules the structure linter reports for each. The pack's code recomputes every result in its CI job.

nouns.title: Record checks for accessibility findings, with synthetic golden findings
nouns.category_reason: Deterministic checks with synthetic known-good and known-bad records; the validator recomputes them.

value.purpose: Checks every accessibility finding must pass before it goes into an audit report: a cited criterion with its name and level, failure or advisory, where it was seen, evidence and a fix. The four synthetic good findings pass; each synthetic bad finding fails exactly the one check named in fails.

deterministic_checks.why: Every finding cites one WCAG success criterion by number.
The criterion's name is written out, so a reader need not look it up.
The criterion's level is A, AA or AAA.
An AA audit never fails a page on an AAA criterion.
Each finding says whether it fails its criterion or is advisory.
The finding names the state, such as a menu open or an error shown.
The finding names the viewport width.
At least one piece of evidence.
Every evidence item says what it is.
A contrast finding records the measured ratio.
A reflow finding is recorded at 320 CSS pixels.
A target size finding records width by height.
The finding says who is affected and how.
The finding suggests a specific fix.
Findings hold no email addresses or phone numbers.

finding.title: Muted footer text is too faint in the dark theme.
finding.measured: 3.69:1 for 14 px text, where 4.5:1 is required

evidence.detail: Foreground #6b7280 on background #0f172a, measured with the pack's contrast tool.
Footer at 390 pixels, dark theme.

finding.impact: People with low vision cannot read the hours and address in the footer at night.
finding.suggested_fix: Use the dark theme's secondary text token, #9ca3af, which measures 7.03:1 on #0f172a.

finding.title: The intro video has no captions.

evidence.detail: The video element has no track element, and no caption file is linked.

finding.impact: Deaf and hard-of-hearing volunteers miss the whole safety briefing.
finding.suggested_fix: Add a WebVTT captions track in English, marked default, timed to the narration, and check a sample of cues against the script.

finding.title: Shift picker arrows are smaller than 24 by 24 pixels and touch each other.
finding.measured: 18 by 18 CSS pixels, 4 pixels apart

evidence.detail: Bounding boxes 18 by 18; the 24-pixel circles around them overlap, so the spacing exception does not apply.

finding.impact: Volunteers with tremors open the wrong week.
finding.suggested_fix: Give each arrow a 44 by 44 pixel hit area with padding, or space them so 24-pixel circles do not touch.

finding.title: The banner animation ignores the reduced motion setting.

evidence.detail: With reduced motion set, the parallax still moves for 1.2 seconds on scroll.

finding.impact: People with vestibular conditions may feel unwell; this is AAA, so it does not fail an AA audit.
finding.suggested_fix: Turn the parallax off under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

finding.title: Muted footer text is too faint in the dark theme.
finding.measured: 3.69:1 for 14 px text, where 4.5:1 is required

evidence.detail: Reported by a volunteer at jo.real@mailbox.net.

finding.impact: People with low vision cannot read the hours and address in the footer at night.
finding.suggested_fix: Use the dark theme's secondary text token, #9ca3af, which measures 7.03:1 on #0f172a.

nouns.title: Template: an accessibility audit plan: pages, states, cells, criteria and what is out of scope
nouns.category_reason: A plan is a testable statement of what the audit will and will not cover.

value.describes: an accessibility audit plan: pages, states, cells, criteria and what is out of scope
rules: widths_px includes 320.
themes lists every theme the surface offers.
Every in-scope criterion maps to a check or to not_in_scope.

nouns.title: Template: screenshots and DOM snapshots of every planned cell, by digest
nouns.category_reason: A capture set is a recorded run of page loads.

value.describes: screenshots and DOM snapshots of every planned cell, by digest
rules: A captured cell has both digests and the image size.
A not_run cell has a reason.
not_run counts the not_run cells.

nouns.title: Template: one check's results across the captured cells, each citing a criterion
nouns.category_reason: A check result is a recorded, repeatable check run.

value.describes: one check's results across the captured cells, each citing a criterion
rules: failed and cannot_tell count those results.
Every fail has measured or evidence_sha256.
Every sc is in the checklist.

nouns.title: Template: a person's session with assistive technology on the key tasks
nouns.category_reason: A session is a recorded run by a person.

value.describes: a person's session with assistive technology on the key tasks
rules: Each technology names its exact version and the browser it ran with.
Every task has notes in the tester's words.

nouns.title: Template: an accessibility audit report with cited findings, a criteria summary and what was not checked
nouns.category_reason: A report is a recorded evaluation of the check results.

value.describes: an accessibility audit report with cited findings, a criteria summary and what was not checked
rules: Every finding passes the audit checks.
statement is failures_found when any finding is a failure.
no_failures_found_in_what_was_checked needs an empty not_checked and a person's assistive-technology session.

nouns.title: Template: a different worker's recheck of a sample of an audit's findings
nouns.category_reason: A review is a recorded verification.

value.describes: a different worker's recheck of a sample of an audit's findings
rules: distinct_from_auditor is true, or the review ends blocked.
At least five findings are sampled, or all when there are fewer.

nouns.category_reason: A synthetic instance in the template's shape.

not_in_scope.why: It books a real shift; no test target was named.

value.shows: A plan with every width and theme, both motion settings, the full checklist and what is out of scope with reasons.
value.source: Synthetic. Written for this pack; every name, address, number and identifier is made up.

nouns.title: Worked example: a keyboard walk with one invisible focus stop
nouns.category_reason: A synthetic instance in the template's shape.

results.note: The first stop is a skip link and Enter moves focus into main.

results.measured: Focused and unfocused crops are identical at all 14 shift buttons.

results.note: Focus left the native video controls after five presses.
No shortcuts are documented; letter keys were not tried on every page.

value.shows: Each result cites its criterion; the failure carries a digest and region; a trap is not reported for native video controls that let focus go.
value.source: Synthetic. Written for this pack; every name, address, number and identifier is made up.

nouns.title: Worked example: an audit report with failures, an advisory and what was not checked
nouns.category_reason: A synthetic instance in the template's shape.

instance.scope: Three pages of the synthetic pantry volunteer site at 1440, 390 and 320 pixels, light and dark.

not_checked.why: The person who runs it is booked for next week.
It books a real shift; no test target was named.

findings.title: Shift buttons show no keyboard focus indicator.
findings.measured: Identical crops focused and unfocused at all 14 buttons.

evidence.detail: Stops 9 to 22 of the walk.

findings.impact: Keyboard-only volunteers cannot tell which shift they are about to choose.
findings.suggested_fix: Add :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px } to the shift buttons.

findings.title: Muted footer text is too faint in the dark theme.
findings.measured: 3.69:1 for 14 px text, where 4.5:1 is required

evidence.detail: Foreground #6b7280 on background #0f172a.

findings.impact: People with low vision cannot read the footer at night.

findings.title: The banner animation ignores the reduced motion setting.

evidence.detail: With reduced motion set, the parallax still moves.

findings.impact: People with vestibular conditions may feel unwell; advisory only.
findings.suggested_fix: Turn the parallax off under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

instance.statement_reason: Two findings fail AA criteria. A screen reader session and the confirmation step were not checked.

value.shows: Findings that pass the audit checks, an AAA advisory that does not fail the page, a summary row per criterion and an honest statement.
value.source: Synthetic. Written for this pack; every name, address, number and identifier is made up.

verbs.title: Plan the accessibility audit
verbs.summary: Name the pages, states, widths, themes, motion settings and input modes to audit, the criteria in scope and what is out of scope, with reasons.
verbs.outcome: An audit plan every check verb can follow.

slots.name: target_brief
slots.description: Pin of a brief naming the surface, its build, its pages and who uses it.

steps: List the pages and the states that matter: as loaded, menus and dialogs opened by keyboard, and error or empty states reachable without real data.
Use the capture matrix for widths, themes, motion settings and input modes; include 320 pixels and every theme the surface offers.
Put every A and AA criterion from the checklist in scope unless the brief narrows it, and list anything left out under not_in_scope with the reason.
Say whether a person's assistive-technology session is planned, and if not, why.

acceptance.check: The plan validates against template.audit-plan's schema.
widths_px includes 320.
Every checklist criterion appears in criteria or in not_in_scope.
The states cover the tasks the brief says people come to do.

verbs.title: Capture every planned state
verbs.summary: Load each planned page in each cell with read-only requests and save a screenshot and a rendered DOM snapshot of every state, by digest.
verbs.outcome: A capture set covering every planned cell or saying why a cell was not run.
steps: Load each page with GET only and reach each planned state by keyboard or links; never submit a form, type into a field or create an account.
Save a full-page screenshot and a rendered DOM snapshot of every cell and record their SHA-256 digests and the image size.
Record a cell as not_run with the reason when reaching its state would need input or an account.

acceptance.check: The capture set validates against template.capture-set's schema.
Every planned cell is captured or not_run with a reason.
Hashing the saved files gives the recorded digests.

network: Read-only page loads of the addresses in the plan with keyboard navigation only; no form is submitted, nothing is typed into fields and no account is created.

verbs.title: Check contrast in every theme
verbs.summary: Measure every text and background pair, control boundary and focus indicator in each captured theme with the contrast tool, and cite 1.4.3 or 1.4.11 for each result.
verbs.outcome: A contrast check result with measured ratios.

slots.name: capture_set
slots.description: Pin of the capture set to check.

steps: Collect each text element's color and its effective background from the computed styles of each captured cell.
Run the contrast tool on every pair, using the large-text rule; record text over images or gradients as cannot_tell unless measured at its lightest and darkest points.
Measure focus indicators and control borders against what is next to them at 3:1 under 1.4.11.
Check text that appears only on focus, such as a skip link, in its focused state.

acceptance.check: The result validates against template.check-result's schema.
Running the pinned tool on the recorded colors gives the recorded ratios.
Every theme in the plan has results.
Every result cites 1.4.3, 1.4.6 or 1.4.11.

verbs.title: Lint landmarks, headings and language
verbs.summary: Run the structure linter on every rendered DOM snapshot and record each landmark, heading-order, language and title result with its criterion.

slots.name: capture_set
slots.description: Pin of the capture set to check.

steps: Run the pinned linter on each snapshot by digest and copy each result with its criterion, level and failure or advisory.
Record language of parts as cannot_tell when a passage looks like another language, for a reader to confirm.

acceptance.check: The result validates against template.check-result's schema.
Running the pinned linter on the snapshots gives the recorded results.
Advisory rules are never recorded as fail of their criterion.

verbs.title: Walk each page with the keyboard
verbs.summary: Tab through each planned page and state, recording every focus stop's visibility, whether it is obscured, the order, traps, the skip link and single-key shortcuts.
verbs.outcome: A keyboard check result with a trace of every stop.
steps: Follow the keyboard procedure at each planned width: Tab and Shift+Tab through every stop and record the evidence it names for each.
Compare crops of each stop focused and unfocused to decide whether the indicator is visible; record the crop digests.
Count presses inside native media controls until focus leaves before calling anything a trap.
Never press Enter on a submit control and never type into a field.

acceptance.check: The result validates against template.check-result's schema.
Every focus-visible fail has a crop digest and region.
The first stop and the skip link's target are recorded for every page.
Each page's focus order is judged against its reading order.

network: Read-only page loads of the addresses in the plan with keyboard navigation only; no form is submitted, nothing is typed into fields and no account is created.

verbs.title: Check reflow and text spacing
verbs.summary: At 320 CSS pixels, record horizontal scrolling and what causes it, exempt only two-dimensional content, and apply the text-spacing values locally to find clipped text.
verbs.outcome: A reflow check result citing 1.4.10, 1.4.12 and 1.4.4.
steps: Load each page at 320 CSS pixels wide and record the page's scroll width and the elements that overflow it.
Name the exception for any overflow inside two-dimensional content, such as a data table or slides, and fail the rest under 1.4.10.
Apply the four text-spacing values in your own browser only and record clipped or overlapping text under 1.4.12, ignoring visually hidden 1-pixel helper text.
Zoom text to 200 percent at 1280 pixels and record lost content under 1.4.4.

acceptance.check: The result validates against template.check-result's schema.
Every page has its scroll width at 320 recorded.
Every overflow marked pass names its two-dimensional exception.

network: Read-only page loads of the addresses in the plan with keyboard navigation only; no form is submitted, nothing is typed into fields and no account is created.

verbs.title: Check pointer target sizes
verbs.summary: Measure every pointer target at the planned widths; pass 24 by 24 CSS pixels, otherwise apply the exceptions in order and record the one used.
verbs.outcome: A target size check result citing 2.5.8.
steps: Measure each link, button and control's clickable box at 390 and 1440 pixels; a label tied to a checkbox adds its area.
Pass targets of at least 24 by 24; for smaller ones apply spacing, equivalent, inline, user agent and essential in that order and record which applied.
Fail a small target only when no exception applies, and record its width by height.

acceptance.check: The result validates against template.check-result's schema.
Every fail records width by height in CSS pixels.
Every target under 24 that passes names its exception.

network: Read-only page loads of the addresses in the plan with keyboard navigation only; no form is submitted, nothing is typed into fields and no account is created.

verbs.title: Check video and audio
verbs.summary: For every video and audio element, check captions, audio description or a media alternative, a transcript, keyboard-operable named controls and sound that starts on its own.
verbs.outcome: A media check result citing 1.2.1, 1.2.2, 1.2.3, 1.2.5 and 1.4.2.
steps: Fetch each caption track read-only and record its kind, language, status, cue count and the time its last cue ends against the media's duration.
Compare a sample of at least ten cues with the script or narration and record mismatches.

Record whether a described version, a descriptions track or a full text alternative exists; if none, record whether the narration conveys the important visuals, and mark that judgment cannot_tell when you could not watch the whole video.
Check that the controls work by keyboard and have names, and that nothing plays sound on its own.

acceptance.check: The result validates against template.check-result's schema.
Every caption track's status, cue count and last cue time are recorded.
The cue sample is compared with the narration or script.

network: Read-only page loads of the addresses in the plan with keyboard navigation only; no form is submitted, nothing is typed into fields and no account is created.

verbs.title: Check motion and the reduced motion setting
verbs.summary: Compare running animations with reduced motion off and on, flag motion longer than five seconds without a pause control, and leave flashing as cannot_tell unless measured.
verbs.outcome: A motion check result citing 2.2.2, 2.3.1 and 2.3.3.
steps: Load each page with prefers-reduced-motion set to no-preference and to reduce, and record running and infinite animations and autoplaying media.
Fail motion that starts on its own and lasts more than five seconds with no pause, stop or hide control under 2.2.2.
Record 2.3.1 as cannot_tell unless a named flash analysis tool measured it, and record reduced-motion support as advisory under 2.3.3.

acceptance.check: The result validates against template.check-result's schema.
Every page has results for both motion settings.
No 2.3.1 result is pass without a named measurement.

network: Read-only page loads of the addresses in the plan with keyboard navigation only; no form is submitted, nothing is typed into fields and no account is created.

verbs.title: Check text alternatives, names and labels
verbs.summary: List images, icons, icon-only controls and fields in each snapshot; check each has a name that serves its purpose, that visible labels are in the name and that fields have labels or instructions.
verbs.outcome: A text alternatives check result citing 1.1.1, 2.5.3, 3.3.2, 4.1.2 and 2.4.4.

slots.name: capture_set
slots.description: Pin of the capture set to check.

steps: List every image, SVG with role img, icon-only button or link, and form field in each snapshot.
Fail missing names under 1.1.1 or 4.1.2, and judge whether each name serves the same purpose; decorative images should be hidden.
Check that each control's accessible name contains its visible label (2.5.3) and that each field has a label, with instructions tied to it when they matter (3.3.2).
Never describe an image you cannot see; mark it cannot_tell.

acceptance.check: The result validates against template.check-result's schema.
The number of listed items equals the number of such elements in the snapshots.
Each passing name serves the same purpose as the image or control.

verbs.title: Try the key tasks with assistive technology
verbs.summary: A person uses a screen reader, and optionally magnification or voice control, to do the planned key tasks and records what happened in their own words. This template performs nothing itself.
steps: Use the exact technology versions you name, with the browser each ran in.
Do each planned task and record completed, completed_with_difficulty, not_completed or not_run, with what was announced where you got stuck.
Use only synthetic data, and never book, buy or create an account.

acceptance.check: The session validates against template.assistive-tech-session's schema.
Every technology entry contains a version number.
Every planned task has a result and notes.

verbs.title: Write the audit report
verbs.summary: Turn the check results into findings that each cite their criterion, summarize every criterion in scope, list what was not checked and derive the statement by the method's rule.
verbs.outcome: An audit report whose findings pass the audit checks.

slots.name: assistive_tech_session
slots.description: Pin of a person's assistive-technology session, if one ran.

steps: Write one finding per distinct problem, grouping repeats of the same pattern, each citing its criterion's number, name and level and whether it fails it.
Give every finding the address, state, width, theme, evidence, who is affected and a specific fix.
Summarize every in-scope criterion as pass, fail, cannot_tell or not_checked, and list everything not checked with the reason.
Derive the statement by the method's rule and never call the site compliant, certified or fully accessible.
Propose findings-to-fixes.record-finding for every failure, with the report pinned as evidence.

acceptance.check: The report validates against template.audit-report's schema.
Every finding passes the pinned audit checks.
Every in-scope criterion appears once in criteria_summary.
The statement follows from the findings, not_checked and whether a session ran.
Each suggested fix says what to change, not only that something should improve.

verbs.title: Review the audit
verbs.summary: A worker other than the auditor reproduces a sample of the findings from their evidence, checks each cited criterion and checks that the statement follows the rule.
verbs.outcome: An audit review accepting, changing or rejecting the report.

slots.name: check_results
slots.description: Pins of the check results it used.

steps: Confirm you wrote none of the report or its check results; otherwise end blocked.
Reproduce at least five findings, or all of them when there are fewer, from their evidence, and record yes, no or could_not for each.
Check that each sampled finding cites the right criterion and level, and that the statement follows the method's rule.

acceptance.check: The review validates against template.audit-review's schema.
At least five findings, or all when fewer, are sampled.
distinct_from_auditor is true.
